sources.title: Top Generative AI Service Providers 2026: Penetration Maturity (PeMa) Quadrant
sources.method: Vendor study. 28 GenAI service providers took part voluntarily through a questionnaire, briefing calls and supporting case material, complemented by secondary research. Each vendor is scored on two normalised 0 to 1 indices, Penetration (market reach) and Maturity (technical and delivery depth), and placed in one of four quadrants.
sources.license_note: Licensed analyst report. We use it as a cited input to our meta-analysis only. No text, images or charts are reproduced. Findings are restated in our own words with page references.
sources.bias_note: Vendor-submitted data is not independently audited by the publisher. Vendors that disclose performance figures (such as POC-to-production rates) tend to be the strong performers, so disclosed metrics are selectively reported.
sources.how_we_use_it: Market findings, delivery challenges, service taxonomy, pricing and engagement benchmarks, and the 28-vendor landscape with scores and quadrant placement.

sources.title: 2026 State of Real-Time Data: Agentic Enterprises Are Running on Real-Time Data
sources.method: Custom survey (IDC Real-Time Data Study) fielded in June 2026. Respondents were scored 0 to 100 on real-time data maturity, blending real-time deployment depth, agentic AI adoption and measurable outcomes, then split into four percentile tiers.
sources.sample: 623 senior technology decision-makers at enterprises with revenue above 1 billion USD, across eight countries, led by manufacturing, financial services and retail. 78 percent are primary decision-makers for real-time data; 71 percent own AI or agentic initiatives.
sources.license_note: IDC InfoBrief licensed by the sponsor for external distribution. We cite the survey results and restate them in our own words. Charts are rebuilt from the published data tables; no source images are reused.
sources.bias_note: Sponsored by Solace, a real-time data platform vendor. The brief's framing (real-time data as the deciding factor for agentic success) aligns with the sponsor's product. The maturity score itself includes real-time deployment as an input, so part of the correlation between maturity and real-time adoption is built in. We report the survey numbers as measured and flag this framing.
sources.how_we_use_it: Buyer-side adoption statistics, maturity-tier comparisons, barriers to scaling agents, technical challenges, and what leading organisations do differently.

sources.title: The State of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI
sources.method: Annual online global survey fielded 4 May to 8 June 2026, with 1,719 participants across 97 countries, industries, company sizes and functions.
sources.license_note: Public report downloaded by the authors from McKinsey's site. Cited and restated in our own words; no text, charts or images reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Self-reported survey of executives; McKinsey also sells AI consulting services. Weighting and respondent mix are as described in the report.
sources.how_we_use_it: Global adoption and scaling rates, agent deployment by function, EBIT impact, high-performer traits, and year-over-year trend.

sources.title: State of AI in the Enterprise: The untapped edge (2026 report)
sources.method: Global survey of 3,235 senior leaders (board, C-suite, president, VP and director level), fielded August to September 2025, split equally between IT and line-of-business leaders across 24 countries.
sources.license_note: Public PDF downloaded from Deloitte's site. Cited and restated in our own words; no text, charts or images reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Self-reported survey; Deloitte sells AI advisory services. Fielded in late 2025, so it predates the 2026 sources by several months.
sources.how_we_use_it: Value realised by type, depth of transformation, barriers (skills, governance), agentic AI potential by function, and governance-value link.

sources.title: BCG AI Radar 2026: As AI Investments Surge, CEOs Take the Lead
sources.method: Survey of 2,360 executives, including 640 CEOs, across 16 markets and nine industries.
sources.license_note: Public PDF fetched from BCG's web assets. Cited and restated in our own words; no text, charts or images reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Self-reported survey; BCG sells AI consulting services.
sources.how_we_use_it: AI investment as a share of revenue, CEO ownership of AI decisions, the value gap, investment resilience, and value-driver breakdown.

sources.title: The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025
sources.method: Multi-method study, January to June 2025: systematic review of more than 300 publicly disclosed AI initiatives, 52 structured interviews, and 153 survey responses from senior leaders gathered at four conferences.
sources.license_note: Official copy obtained by the authors from MIT NANDA. Cited and restated in our own words; no text, charts or images reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Small and convenience-based survey sample; the headline 95 percent figure has been widely quoted and debated. Preliminary version (v0.1) of the report. Predates the 2026 sources by a year.
sources.how_we_use_it: The pilot-to-production 'divide', reasons pilots stall (lack of learning and context), buy-versus-build outcomes, and shadow AI usage.

sources.title: 2025: The State of Generative AI in the Enterprise
sources.method: Survey of about 495 US enterprise AI decision-makers, fielded 7 to 25 November 2025, combined with Menlo's own market sizing.
sources.license_note: Public web article. Cited and restated in our own words; no text or charts reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Published by a venture capital firm with investments in AI companies; market-share figures are estimates.
sources.how_we_use_it: Enterprise GenAI spend and growth, spend by layer and department, buy-versus-build split, and vendor share shifts.

sources.title: Leaders, gainers and unexpected winners in the enterprise AI arms race (third annual CIO survey)
sources.method: Third-party survey of 100 VPs and C-level executives at Global 2000 companies (88 percent above 1 billion USD revenue), run through an independent expert network, published 30 January 2026.
sources.license_note: Public web article. Cited and restated in our own words; no text or charts reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Published by a venture capital firm with investments in AI companies. Small sample.
sources.how_we_use_it: Enterprise AI budget per company and growth, multi-model strategies, buy-versus-build, and application adoption.

sources.title: AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q2 2026
sources.method: Quarterly survey of 204 US C-suite and business leaders at organisations with annual revenue of 1 billion USD or more, fielded 28 April to 25 May 2026.
sources.license_note: Public PDF downloaded from KPMG's site. Cited and restated in our own words; no text, charts or images reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Small US-only sample; KPMG sells AI advisory services. Quarter-over-quarter comparisons rely on separate samples.
sources.how_we_use_it: Most recent agent deployment and scaling rates, employee adoption of agents, and the shift toward cost visibility and governance.

sources.title: 2026 Work Trend Index Annual Report
sources.method: Survey of 20,000 workers using AI across 10 countries, combined with anonymised Microsoft 365 productivity signals and analysis of more than 100,000 Copilot conversations.
sources.license_note: Public PDF downloaded from Microsoft's site. Cited and restated in our own words; no text, charts or images reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Vendor-published research from a company selling AI products; usage signals come from its own platform. Treated like the Solace-sponsored IDC brief.
sources.how_we_use_it: Workforce-side adoption, the organisational readiness gap, and how work is being redesigned around agents.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Index Report 2026
sources.method: Annual compilation of indicators from academic, industry and government sources across nine chapters. We use the Economy and Public Opinion chapters only.
sources.sample: Compiled indicators; underlying surveys vary by indicator
sources.license_note: Public PDF downloaded from Stanford HAI. Cited and restated in our own words; no text, charts or images reproduced.
sources.bias_note: Academic and broadly neutral. Many of its business indicators are themselves drawn from surveys by McKinsey and others, so it is not fully independent of src-03.
sources.how_we_use_it: Organisational adoption rates, corporate investment, productivity evidence, and public opinion on AI.

sources.title: FutureScape 2026: Moving into the agentic future (public summary)
sources.method: Public blog summary of IDC's FutureScape 2026 predictions (35 prediction sets across 12 industries). The full prediction documents are for IDC subscribers and were not used.
sources.license_note: Public web summary only. Cited and restated in our own words.
sources.bias_note: Summary-only source with lower evidence weight. Predictions, not measurements.
sources.how_we_use_it: Forward-looking predictions on agentic AI adoption and spending, used in the outlook section only.
